sol_sql: WITH tech_signals AS ( SELECT s.SignalRegistry, s.TelescRef, p.TechSigProb * ( 1 - p.NatSrcProb ) * p.SigUnique * ( 0.5 + p.AnomScore / 10 ) AS TOLS, s.BwHz / ( s.CenterFreqMhz * 1000000 ) AS BFR FROM Signals AS s JOIN SignalProbabilities AS p ON s.SignalRegistry = p.SignalRef WHERE p.TechSigProb > 0.7 AND p.NatSrcProb < 0.3 AND p.ArtSrcProb < 50 AND s.BwHz / ( s.CenterFreqMhz * 1000000 ) < 0.001 ) SELECT t.ObservStation, COUNT(*) AS potential_tech_signals, AVG(ts.TOLS) AS avg_tols, AVG(ts.BFR) AS avg_bfr, COUNT(*) * 100.0 / ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tech_signals ) AS percentage_of_total FROM tech_signals AS ts JOIN Telescopes AS t ON ts.TelescRef = t.TelescRegistry GROUP BY t.ObservStation ORDER BY potential_tech_signals DESC NULLS FIRST

Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator (SNQI).description: Combines SNR and noise floor to provide a unified signal quality metric.
Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator (SNQI).definition: $\text{SNQI} = \text{SnrRatio} - 0.1 \times |\text{NoiseFloorDbm}|$, where higher values indicate better detection quality. Positive values generally indicate analyzable signals.

Atmospheric Observability Index (AOI).description: Quantifies how conducive atmospheric conditions are for signal detection.
Atmospheric Observability Index (AOI).definition: $\text{AOI} = \text{AtmosTransparency} \times (1 - \frac{\text{HumidityRate}}{100}) \times (1 - 0.02 \times \text{WindSpeedMs})$, where values closer to 1 indicate ideal observation conditions.

Signal Complexity Ratio (SCR).description: Measures the relationship between signal complexity and information density.
Signal Complexity Ratio (SCR).definition: $\text{SCR} = \frac{\text{ComplexIdx} \times \text{InfoDense}}{\log(\text{BwHz})}$, where higher values suggest potential artificial origin rather than natural phenomena.

Technological Origin Likelihood Score (T.description: Combines multiple factors to estimate likelihood of technological origin.
Technological Origin Likelihood Score (T.definition: $\text{TOLS} = \text{TechSigProb} \times (1 - \text{NatSrcProb}) \times \text{SigUnique} \times (0.5 + \frac{\text{AnomScore}}{10})$, where values above 0.75 warrant further investigation as potential technosignatures.

Bandwidth-Frequency Ratio (BFR).description: Measures the proportion of bandwidth to center frequency, helping identify signal type.
Bandwidth-Frequency Ratio (BFR).definition: $\text{BFR} = \frac{\text{BwHz}}{\text{CenterFreqMhz} \times 10^6}$, where narrow ratios ($<0.001$) often indicate technological signals while wider ratios suggest natural phenomena.

Detection Instrument Sensitivity Factor.description: Calculates the effective sensitivity of the detection setup based on telescope and environmental factors.
Detection Instrument Sensitivity Factor.definition: $\text{DISF} = (10 - \frac{|\text{AirTempC} - 15|}{10}) \times \text{AtmosTransparency} \times (1 - \frac{\text{HumidityRate}}{200}) \times \frac{100 - \text{LunarDistDeg}}{100}$, where values closer to 10 indicate optimal detection sensitivity.

Encoding Complexity Index (ECI).description: Evaluates the sophistication of potential encoding in the signal.
Encoding Complexity Index (ECI).definition: $\text{ECI} = \frac{\text{CompressRatio} \times \text{ComplexIdx} \times \text{EntropyVal}}{10}$, where values above 1.5 suggest deliberate information encoding rather than random patterns.

Signal Stability Metric (SSM).description: Quantifies overall temporal and spectral stability of a signal.
Signal Stability Metric (SSM).definition: $\text{SSM} = (1 - \frac{|\text{FreqDriftHzs}|}{\text{FreqMhz} \times 1000}) \times \frac{\text{SigDurSec}}{1 + \frac{\text{DoppShiftHz}}{1000}}$, where higher values indicate more stable signals typical of fixed transmitters.

Research Priority Index (RPI).description: Helps researchers prioritize signals for follow-up based on multiple factors.
Research Priority Index (RPI).definition: $\text{RPI} = (\text{TechSigProb} \times 4 + \frac{\text{BioSigProb}}{100} + \text{SigUnique} \times 2 + \frac{\text{AnomScore}}{2}) \times (1 - \text{FalsePosProb})$, where values above 3 indicate high research priority.

Lunar Interference Factor (LIF).description: Calculates the potential interference from lunar illumination on observations.
Lunar Interference Factor (LIF).definition: $\text{LIF} = (1 - \frac{\text{LunarDistDeg}}{180}) \times (1 - \text{AtmosTransparency})$, where higher values indicate more lunar interference. Values above 0.5 suggest significant lunar contamination in data.

Technosignature.description: Defines the concept of signals that indicate technological activity.
Technosignature.definition: A signal with $\text{TechSigProb} > 0.7$, $\text{NatSrcProb} < 0.3$, and $\text{ArtSrcProb} < 50$ that exhibits narrow bandwidth ($\text{BFR} < 0.001$) and high information density ($\text{InfoDense} > 0.8$).

Coherent Information Pattern (CIP).description: Identifies signals showing patterns consistent with deliberate information transmission.
Coherent Information Pattern (CIP).definition: Signals characterized by high signal stability ($\text{SSM} > 0.8$), organized information structure ($\text{EntropyVal}$ between 0.4-0.8), and consistent modulation ($\text{ModType}$ with $\text{ModIndex} > 0.5$).

Target of Opportunity (TOO).description: Identifies high-value signals requiring immediate follow-up observation.
Target of Opportunity (TOO).definition: Any signal with $\text{RPI} > 3.5$, $\text{TechSigProb} > 0.8$, and $\text{AnomScore} > 5$ that has not been previously documented or explained by known phenomena.

Optimal Observing Window (OOW).description: Defines conditions when observational quality is maximized.
Optimal Observing Window (OOW).definition: Time periods when $\text{AOI} > 0.85$, $\text{LunarStage}$ is 'New' or 'First Quarter', $\text{LunarDistDeg} > 45$, and $\text{SolarStatus}$ is 'Low' or 'Moderate'.

Signal Degradation Scenario (SDS).description: Characterizes situations where signal quality is compromised by environmental factors.
Signal Degradation Scenario (SDS).definition: Observation conditions where one or more of: $\text{AtmosTransparency} < 0.7$, $\text{HumidityRate} > 70$, $\text{WindSpeedMs} > 8$, or $\text{GeomagStatus}$ contains 'Storm', resulting in compromised data quality.

Narrowband Technological Marker (NTM).description: Identifies a specific signature associated with technological transmission.
Narrowband Technological Marker (NTM).definition: Signals with extremely narrow bandwidth ($\text{BFR} < 0.0001$), stable frequency ($\text{FreqDriftHzs} < 0.1$).

Observational Confidence Level (OCL).description: Rates the reliability of observations based on conditions and equipment.
Observational Confidence Level (OCL).definition: A classification system with three tiers: 'High' ($\text{AOI} > 0.8$, $\text{EquipStatus} = \text{'Operational'}$, $\text{CalibrStatus} = \text{'Current'}$), 'Medium' ($\text{AOI}$ 0.5-0.8, minor equipment issues), and 'Low' ($\text{AOI} < 0.5$ or significant equipment problems).

Potential Biosignature.description: Defines characteristics of signals potentially associated with biological processes.
Potential Biosignature.definition: Signals with $\text{BioSigProb} > 0.6$, $\text{TechSigProb} < 0.4$, and spectral features that match known biological emission patterns, often associated with specific molecular transitions.

Encoded Information Transfer (EIT).description: Characterizes signals that appear to contain deliberate information encoding.
Encoded Information Transfer (EIT).definition: Signals with $\text{ECI} > 1.8$, $\text{EntropyVal}$ between 0.3-0.7 (not random but structured), and consistent internal patterns that suggest language or data encoding schemes.

Fast Radio Transient (FRT).description: Defines a specific class of brief, high-energy radio emissions.
Fast Radio Transient (FRT).definition: Signals with extremely short duration ($\text{SigDurSec} < 0.1$), high signal strength ($\text{SigStrDb} > 15$), broad bandwidth ($\text{BwHz} > 1000000$), and no periodicity ($\text{RepeatCount} = 1$).

WeathProfile: Clear.description: Illustrates optimal weather conditions for signal detection.
WeathProfile: Clear.definition: Indicates pristine sky conditions with no clouds, usually associated with $\text{AtmosTransparency} > 0.9$, low $\text{HumidityRate} (< 40\%)$, and minimal $\text{WindSpeedMs} (< 3.0)$. Provides ideal visibility for optical observations and minimal atmospheric interference for radio observations.

SeeingProfile: Excellent.definition: Describes atmospheric conditions with minimal turbulence, allowing for sharp, detailed observations. Typically corresponds to image stability better than 1 arcsecond and is often associated with stable temperature gradients and low wind speeds ($\text{WindSpeedMs} < 2.5$).

SignalClass: Narrowband.description: Illustrates characteristics of narrowband signal detections.
SignalClass: Narrowband.definition: Describes signals occupying a very narrow portion of the spectrum (typically $\text{BFR} < 0.0001$). Often associated with technological origins as natural sources rarely produce such spectrally confined emissions. These signals are particularly interesting in SETI research.

GeomagStatus: Major Storm.definition: Indicates intense solar-induced geomagnetic activity with Kp index ≥ 7. During such conditions, ionospheric perturbations significantly affect radio observations below 100 MHz, aurora may be visible at mid-latitudes, and satellite communications may experience disruptions.

CIP Classification Label.description: Three-tier rating system for evaluating signal coherence against intelligent transmission criteria.
CIP Classification Label.definition: Classification labels: 'Coherent Information Pattern Detected' ($\text{SSM} > 0.8$, $\text{EntropyVal}$ between 0.4-0.8, and $\text{ModIndex} > 0.5$), 'Potential Information Pattern' ($\text{SSM} > 0.6$ and $\text{EntropyVal}$ between 0.3-0.9$), or 'No Clear Pattern' (all other signals).

SigClassType: Broadband Transient.description: Illustrates a class of brief signals covering wide frequency ranges.
SigClassType: Broadband Transient.definition: Describes short-duration signals ($\text{SigDurSec}$ typically $< 5$) that span a large portion of the spectrum ($\text{BFR} > 0.1$). Examples include solar radio bursts, lightning discharges, and certain types of cosmic explosions like Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs).

PolarMode: Circular.description: Illustrates circular polarization in detected signals.
PolarMode: Circular.definition: Describes electromagnetic waves where the electric field vector rotates in a circular pattern as the wave propagates. Circular polarization maintaining high purity across frequency (indicated by $\text{PolarAngleDeg}$ stability) is rare in natural sources and may indicate technological origin.

EncryptEvid: Strong Pattern.description: Illustrates characteristics suggesting deliberate signal encoding.
EncryptEvid: Strong Pattern.definition: Indicates detection of non-random, internally consistent patterns that resist simple decoding but show hallmarks of designed encryption or encoding. Characterized by high $\text{EntropyVal} (> 0.7)$ combined with structural regularity that defies natural explanation.

EncodeType: Frequency Hopping.description: Illustrates a sophisticated encoding method used in telecommunications.
EncodeType: Frequency Hopping.definition: Describes a transmission technique where the signal rapidly switches frequencies according to a predetermined sequence. Detection would be characterized by discontinuous spectral features that follow a pattern. This technique is used on Earth to secure communications and reduce interference.

FalsePosProb: <0.01.description: Illustrates extremely high confidence in signal detection.
FalsePosProb: <0.01.definition: Indicates less than 1% probability that the signal is a false detection or artifact. Such low false positive probability typically results from multiple independent confirmations, excellent signal strength (high $\text{SnrRatio}$), and elimination of all known terrestrial and instrumental sources.

Modulation Complexity Score (MCS).description: Quantifies the sophistication of signal modulation based on type and stability.
Modulation Complexity Score (MCS).definition: $\text{MCS} = \text{ModIndex} \times (1 + \text{SSM}) \times M_{\text{factor}}$, where $M_{\text{factor}}$ is 2 for $\text{ModType} = \text{'AM'}$, 1.5 for 'FM', and 1 for other types. Incorporates Signal Stability Metric (SSM) to weight stable modulations higher.

Artificial Intelligence Detection Probab.description: Calculates likelihood of artificial intelligence origin based on encoding complexity and technosignature indicators.
Artificial Intelligence Detection Probab.definition: $\text{AIDP} = \frac{\text{ECI} \times \text{TOLS}}{1 + \text{NatSrcProb}}$, where ECI (Encoding Complexity Index) and TOLS (Technological Origin Likelihood Score) are weighted against natural source probability.

Observation Quality Factor (OQF).description: Provides a comprehensive measure of observational conditions quality.
Observation Quality Factor (OQF).definition: $\text{OQF} = \text{AOI} \times (1 - \text{LIF}) \times (\text{PointAccArc} < 2 ? 1 : \frac{2}{\text{PointAccArc}})$, where AOI (Atmospheric Observability Index) and LIF (Lunar Interference Factor) are combined with telescope pointing accuracy.

Information Entropy Ratio (IER).description: Compares signal entropy to expected natural background entropy.
Information Entropy Ratio (IER).definition: $\text{IER} = \frac{\text{EntropyVal}}{\text{NatSrcProb} \times 0.9 + 0.1}$, where values significantly greater than 1 suggest non-natural information content. Uses NatSrcProb as a baseline for expected natural entropy.

Signal Processing Efficiency Index (SPEI.description: Evaluates the computational efficiency of signal processing relative to complexity.
Signal Processing Efficiency Index (SPEI.definition: $\text{SPEI} = \frac{\text{DecodeIters} \times \text{ProcTimeHrs}}{\text{ECI} \times \text{ComplexIdx}}$, where ECI (Encoding Complexity Index) provides the complexity component to normalize processing time and iterations.

Celestial Location Significance Factor (.description: Calculates significance of signal source location based on astronomical targets of interest.
Celestial Location Significance Factor (.definition: $\text{CLSF} = (\text{CelestObj} ? 2 : 1) \times (\text{ObjType} == \text{'Giant'} \&\& \text{ObjMassSol} \text{ between } 0.8 \text{ and } 1.2 ? 1.5 : 1) \times (\text{ObjMetal} > 0 ? \text{ObjMetal} + 1 : 0.5)$, where higher values indicate source locations more likely to harbor intelligent life.

Confirmation Confidence Score (CCS).description: Quantifies overall confidence in signal verification across multiple parameters.
Confirmation Confidence Score (CCS).definition: $\text{CCS} = (1 - \text{FalsePosProb}) \times \text{DecodeConf} \times \text{ClassConf} \times (\text{SNQI} > 0 ? \frac{\text{SNQI}}{10} + 0.5 : 0.1)$, where SNQI (Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator) provides a quality weighting factor.

Habitable Zone Signal Relevance (HZSR).description: Assesses signal relevance based on source's position in habitable zone.
Habitable Zone Signal Relevance (HZSR).definition: $\text{HZSR} = \text{TOLS} \times (\text{ObjType} == \text{'Dwarf'} ? (0.7 \leq \text{ObjMassSol} \leq 1.4 ? (0.8 \leq \frac{\text{SourceDistLy}}{\sqrt{\text{ObjMassSol}}} \leq 1.7 ? 2 : 0.5) : 0.3) : 0.1)$, where TOLS (Technological Origin Likelihood Score) is weighted by stellar habitability factors.

Pattern Recognition Confidence (PRC).description: Measures confidence in identified signal patterns based on multiple factors.
Pattern Recognition Confidence (PRC).definition: $\text{PRC} = (\text{RepeatCount} > 1 ? 1 + \log_{10}(\text{RepeatCount}) : 0.5) \times (\text{EntropyVal} < 0.9 ? 1 : 0.3) \times \text{SCR}$, where SCR (Signal Complexity Ratio) provides complexity weighting.

NTM Classification System.description: A tiered classification system for Narrowband Technological Markers based on signal characteristics.
NTM Classification System.definition: Three-tier classification: 'Strong NTM' (BFR < 0.0001 AND FreqDriftHzs < 0.1 AND non-natural modulation), 'Moderate NTM' (BFR < 0.0005 AND FreqDriftHzs < 0.5 AND non-natural modulation), and 'Not NTM' (all other signals).

High-Confidence Technosignature.description: Defines signals with extremely high likelihood of technological origin.
High-Confidence Technosignature.definition: A Technosignature with $\text{CCS} > 0.9$, $\text{MCS} > 1.5$, and $\text{AIDP} > 0.8$, indicating a signal that meets the basic Technosignature criteria with additional confirmation through modulation complexity and artificial intelligence detection markers.

Habitable Zone Transmission.description: Identifies signals originating from stellar habitable zones with technological characteristics.
Habitable Zone Transmission.definition: A signal with $\text{HZSR} > 1.5$ and Technosignature characteristics, originating from a star system with conditions potentially suitable for life, making it a priority candidate for SETI research.

Multi-Channel Communication Protocol.description: Identifies signal patterns consistent with sophisticated communication protocols.
Multi-Channel Communication Protocol.definition: Signal exhibiting Coherent Information Pattern (CIP) characteristics across multiple frequency channels with coordinated timing ($\text{RepeatCount} > 3$, $\text{PeriodSec}$ consistent across observations) and $\text{ECI} > 2.0$, suggesting a designed communication system.

Quantum-Coherent Transmission.description: Describes signals potentially employing quantum properties for communication.
Quantum-Coherent Transmission.definition: Signals with $\text{QuantEffects}$ containing 'Significant' or 'Observed' patterns, exhibiting unusually high information density ($\text{InfoDense} > 1.5$) while maintaining an $\text{ECI} > 2.5$, suggesting advanced transmission technologies beyond conventional radiofrequency methods.

Research Critical Signal.description: Defines signals requiring immediate and extensive scientific resources.
Research Critical Signal.definition: Signals meeting Target of Opportunity (TOO) criteria with additional $\text{PRC} > 0.8$ and $\text{IMDF} < 0.5$, indicating high-quality, minimally distorted signals that show recognizable patterns warranting priority allocation of research resources.

Directed Transmission.description: Identifies signals that appear specifically directed rather than omnidirectional.
Directed Transmission.definition: Signals with high spatial stability ($\text{SpatStab} = \text{'Moderate'}$), narrow beam characteristics ($\text{PolarMode} = \text{'Linear'}$ with stable $\text{PolarAngleDeg}$), and high $\text{TOLS} > 0.85$, suggesting intentional transmission toward our location.

Signal of Galactic Significance.description: Classifies signals with potential importance to galactic civilization models.
Signal of Galactic Significance.definition: Signals originating from regions of high $\text{CLSF} (> 2.0)$ that display Technosignature characteristics and have $\text{AIDP} > 0.7$, representing potential evidence of advanced civilizations at galactic-relevant locations.

CCS Approximation.description: Simplified CCS calculation using direct signal-to-noise ratio values when full Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator (SNQI) data is unavailable.

Observation-Verified Signal.description: Defines signals that have undergone rigorous verification processes.
Observation-Verified Signal.definition: Signals observed under Optimal Observing Window (OOW) conditions with $\text{OQF} > 0.85$ and $\text{CCS} > 0.8$, indicating high-quality observations with multiple verification methods applied.

Anomalous Quantum Signal.description: Describes signals exhibiting quantum properties inconsistent with current physics models.
Anomalous Quantum Signal.definition: Signals with $\text{QuantEffects}$ indicating anomalous behavior, $\text{AnomScore} > 8$, and unusually high $\text{MCS} (> 2.0)$, suggesting either unknown natural quantum phenomena or extremely advanced transmission technologies beyond current human capabilities.

Analyzable Signals.description: Signals of sufficient quality to be considered useful for further analysis.
Analyzable Signals.definition: Signals with SNQI > 0 are considered analyzable.

Bandwidth-to-Frequency Ratio (BFR).description: Normalized signal width relative to its central frequency.
Bandwidth-to-Frequency Ratio (BFR).definition: $\text{BFR} = \frac{\text{BwHz}}{\text{CenterFreqMhz} \times 1{,}000{,}000}$, used to characterize signal spread relative to its frequency band.

TOLS Category.description: Classification of signals based on TOLS thresholds.
TOLS Category.definition: Categorized as 'Low' if TOLS < 0.25, 'Medium' if TOLS < 0.75, and 'High' otherwise.

High Lunar Interference Events.definition: Events where the calculated LIF is greater than 0.5, indicating strong lunar contamination in the data.

High Confidence Signals.description: Signal with Confirmation Confidence Score (CCS) > 0.8, indicating high reliability.

Equipment Problems.description: Defines what counts as an abnormal condition for a telescope’s subsystems.
Equipment Problems.definition: A telescope is considered to have an equipment problem whenever **any** of its key subsystem states are not in their nominal condition: • Equipment status is not “Operational”; • Calibration status is not “Current”; • Cooling-system status is not “Normal”.

pred_sqls:
WITH tech_signals AS (
  SELECT
    t.observstation AS observatory_name,
    p.techsigprob * (1 - p.natsrcprob) * p.sigunique * (0.5 + p.anomscore / 10) AS tols,
    s.bwhz / (s.centerfreqmhz * 1000000) AS bfr
  FROM signals s
  JOIN signalprobabilities p ON s.signalregistry = p.signalref
  JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
  WHERE p.techsigprob > 0.7
    AND p.natsrcprob < 0.3
    AND p.artsrcprob < 50
    AND s.bwhz / (s.centerfreqmhz * 1000000) < 0.001
),
total_count AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM tech_signals
)
SELECT
  ts.observatory_name,
  COUNT(*) AS technosignature_count,
  AVG(ts.tols) AS avg_tols,
  AVG(ts.bfr) AS avg_bfr,
  COUNT(*) * 100.0 / tc.total AS percentage_of_all_technosignatures
FROM tech_signals ts, total_count tc
GROUP BY ts.observatory_name
ORDER BY technosignature_count DESC;

column_meanings.alien|observatories|observstation: Full name: 'Observatory Name'. Explanation: This field holds the name or unique identifier for the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
column_meanings.alien|observatories|weathprofile: Full name: 'Weather Profile'. Explanation: A short description of weather conditions during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Clear, Cloudy, Partially Cloudy.
column_meanings.alien|observatories|seeingprofile: Full name: 'Seeing Profile'. Explanation: Assessment of sky seeing conditions (atmospheric steadiness). Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
column_meanings.alien|observatories|atmostransparency: Full name: 'Atmospheric Transparency'. Explanation: A numeric measure of how transparent the atmosphere is. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.867'.
column_meanings.alien|observatories|lunarstage: Full name: 'Lunar Phase'. Explanation: The current phase of the Moon during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: First Quarter, Full, Last Quarter, New.
column_meanings.alien|observatories|lunardistdeg: Full name: 'Moon Distance (Degrees)'. Explanation: Angular distance to the Moon in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '97.52'.
column_meanings.alien|observatories|solarstatus: Full name: 'Solar Activity'. Explanation: The level of solar activity at the time of observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Moderate.
column_meanings.alien|observatories|geomagstatus: Full name: 'Geomagnetic Activity'. Explanation: The level of geomagnetic activity during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Active, Quiet, Storm.
column_meanings.alien|observatories|sidereallocal: Full name: 'Local Sidereal Time'. Explanation: Sidereal time at the observatory in HH:MM:SS format. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: '12:34:56'.
column_meanings.alien|observatories|airtempc: Full name: 'Air Temperature (°C)'. Explanation: Ambient temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '18.45'.
column_meanings.alien|observatories|humidityrate: Full name: 'Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Relative humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '62.300'.
column_meanings.alien|observatories|windspeedms: Full name: 'Wind Speed (m/s)'. Explanation: Wind speed in meters per second. Data type: NUMERIC(4,2). Example: '3.45'.
column_meanings.alien|observatories|presshpa: Full name: 'Pressure (hPa)'. Explanation: Atmospheric pressure in hectopascals. Data type: DECIMAL(6,1). Example: '1013.2'.
column_meanings.alien|telescopes|telescregistry: Full name: 'Telescope Registry'. Explanation: A unique identifier for the telescope. Data type: CHAR(20). Example: 'TELESC_0001'.
column_meanings.alien|telescopes|observstation: Full name: 'Observatory Name Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key linking to the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
column_meanings.alien|telescopes|equipstatus: Full name: 'Equipment Status'. Explanation: Operational state of the telescope. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Degraded, Maintenance, Operational.
column_meanings.alien|telescopes|calibrstatus: Full name: 'Calibration Status'. Explanation: Status of telescope’s calibration. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Current, Due, Overdue.
column_meanings.alien|telescopes|pointaccarc: Full name: 'Pointing Accuracy (arcsec)'. Explanation: How precise the telescope can point, in arcseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '0.45'.
column_meanings.alien|telescopes|trackaccarc: Full name: 'Tracking Accuracy (arcsec)'. Explanation: How accurately the telescope can track a target, in arcseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '1.20'.
column_meanings.alien|telescopes|focusquality: Full name: 'Focus Quality'. Explanation: Quality of the telescope’s focusing system. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
column_meanings.alien|telescopes|detecttempk: Full name: 'Detector Temperature (K)'. Explanation: Temperature of the telescope’s primary detector in Kelvin. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '123.45'.
column_meanings.alien|telescopes|coolsysstatus: Full name: 'Cooling System Status'. Explanation: Status of the telescope’s cooling system. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Critical, Normal, Warning.
column_meanings.alien|telescopes|powerstatus: Full name: 'Power Supply Status'. Explanation: Indicates which power source or level is in use. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Backup, Critical, Main.
column_meanings.alien|telescopes|datastorstatus: Full name: 'Data Storage Status'. Explanation: Capacity and status of local data storage. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Available, Critical, Low.
column_meanings.alien|telescopes|netstatus: Full name: 'Network Status'. Explanation: Status of the network connection for telescope data transfer. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Connected, Disconnected, Limited.
column_meanings.alien|telescopes|bandusagepct: Full name: 'Bandwidth Usage (%)'. Explanation: Network bandwidth usage as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '73.25'.
column_meanings.alien|telescopes|procqueuestatus: Full name: 'Processing Queue Status'. Explanation: Indicates how full the processing queue is. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Empty, Full, Normal.
column_meanings.alien|signals|signalregistry: Full name: 'Signal Registry'. Explanation: Unique ID for each signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-123E4567-E89B'.
column_meanings.alien|signals|timemark: Full name: 'Timestamp'. Explanation: The moment of signal detection. In some CSVs, it may be stored as an Excel serial date/time (e.g., '44302.55648' ≈ 2021-05-16 13:20:20 UTC). Data type: TIMESTAMPTZ. Example: '2025-08-01 13:45:00+00'.

column_meanings.alien|signals|sigstrdb: Full name: 'Signal Strength (dB)'. Explanation: Measured strength of the signal in decibels. Data type: NUMERIC(7,2). Example: '12.35'.
column_meanings.alien|signals|freqmhz: Full name: 'Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Signal’s nominal frequency in MHz. Data type: DECIMAL(9,3). Example: '1420.405'.
column_meanings.alien|signals|bwhz: Full name: 'Bandwidth (Hz)'. Explanation: Signal’s bandwidth in Hertz. Data type: DECIMAL(10,3). Example: '500000.000'.
column_meanings.alien|signals|centerfreqmhz: Full name: 'Center Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Center frequency of the detected signal in MHz. Data type: NUMERIC(8,3). Example: '1420.500'.
column_meanings.alien|signals|freqdrifthzs: Full name: 'Frequency Drift (Hz/s)'. Explanation: How fast the signal drifts in frequency over time. Data type: NUMERIC(9,3). Example: '0.123'.
column_meanings.alien|signals|doppshifthz: Full name: 'Doppler Shift (Hz)'. Explanation: Measured Doppler shift of the signal in Hertz. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: '142.75'.
column_meanings.alien|signals|sigdursec: Full name: 'Signal Duration (s)'. Explanation: Total duration of the signal in seconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '12.50'.
column_meanings.alien|signals|pulsepersec: Full name: 'Pulse Rate (pulses/sec)'. Explanation: Rate of pulse repetition in the signal. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '4.500'.
column_meanings.alien|signals|pulsewidms: Full name: 'Pulse Width (ms)'. Explanation: Duration of each pulse in milliseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '2.300'.
column_meanings.alien|signals|modtype: Full name: 'Modulation Type'. Explanation: The method of signal modulation. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: AM, FM, PM, QAM, Unknown.
column_meanings.alien|signals|modindex: Full name: 'Modulation Index'. Explanation: Numerical index describing modulation depth. Data type: DECIMAL(6,4). Example: '0.2875'.
column_meanings.alien|signals|carrierfreqmhz: Full name: 'Carrier Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Frequency of the carrier wave in MHz. Data type: DECIMAL(9,3). Example: '1000.000'.
column_meanings.alien|signals|phaseshiftdeg: Full name: 'Phase Shift (°)'. Explanation: Phase shift in degrees for the signal. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '45.00'.
column_meanings.alien|signals|polarmode: Full name: 'Polarization Mode'. Explanation: Type of signal polarization. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Circular, Elliptical, Linear, Unknown.
column_meanings.alien|signals|polarangledeg: Full name: 'Polarization Angle (°)'. Explanation: Angle of polarization in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(5,1). Example: '90.0'.

column_meanings.alien|signals|atmointerf: Full name: 'Atmospheric Interference'. Explanation: Impact of atmospheric conditions on signal. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.

column_meanings.alien|signalclassification|sigpattern: Full name: 'Signal Pattern'. Explanation: Pattern observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: Periodic, Random, Structured, Unknown.
column_meanings.alien|signalclassification|repeatcount: Full name: 'Repetition Count'. Explanation: Number of times the signal has repeated. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '3'.
column_meanings.alien|signalclassification|periodsec: Full name: 'Period (s)'. Explanation: Duration of each cycle if periodic. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '12.345'.
column_meanings.alien|signalclassification|complexidx: Full name: 'Complexity Index'. Explanation: Numeric measure of the signal’s complexity. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '5.678'.
column_meanings.alien|signalclassification|entropyval: Full name: 'Entropy'. Explanation: Entropy measurement of the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.45'.
column_meanings.alien|signalclassification|infodense: Full name: 'Information Density'. Explanation: Estimated information per unit time/frequency. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.345'.
column_meanings.alien|signalclassification|classconf: Full name: 'Classification Confidence (%)'. Explanation: How confident we are in the assigned signal class. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '92.50'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldecoding|signalref: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal entry. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-GHI-9012'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldecoding|encodetype: Full name: 'Encoding Type'. Explanation: The type of signal encoding used (e.g., Binary). Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Binary, Complex, Tertiary, Unknown.
column_meanings.alien|signaldecoding|compressratio: Full name: 'Compression Ratio'. Explanation: Factor by which the raw signal data was compressed. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.500'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldecoding|errcorrlvl: Full name: 'Error Correction Level'. Explanation: Degree of error correction applied. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
column_meanings.alien|signaldecoding|decodeconf: Full name: 'Decoding Confidence (%)'. Explanation: Confidence level that the decoding is correct. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '88.75'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldecoding|decodemethod: Full name: 'Decoding Method'. Explanation: Method used to decode the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: FFT, Neural Network, Quantum, Wavelet.
column_meanings.alien|signaldecoding|decodestat: Full name: 'Decoding Status'. Explanation: Status of the decoding process. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Failed, In Progress.
column_meanings.alien|signaldecoding|decodeiters: Full name: 'Decoding Iterations'. Explanation: Number of algorithmic passes attempted. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '7'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldecoding|proctimehrs: Full name: 'Processing Time (hours)'. Explanation: Total hours spent decoding. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.50'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldecoding|compresources: Full name: 'Computational Resources'. Explanation: Level of computing power used. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Extreme, High, Low, Medium.
column_meanings.alien|signaldecoding|analysisdp: Full name: 'Analysis Depth'. Explanation: How thoroughly the signal was analyzed. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Comprehensive, Detailed, Preliminary.
column_meanings.alien|signaldecoding|veriflvl: Full name: 'Verification Level'. Explanation: Extent to which decoding has been verified. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Partially, Unverified, Verified.
column_meanings.alien|signaldecoding|confirmstat: Full name: 'Confirmation Status'. Explanation: Whether the decoding results have been confirmed. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Confirmed, Pending, Rejected.
column_meanings.alien|signaldynamics|signalref: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-JKL-3456'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldynamics|sigintegrity: Full name: 'Signal Integrity'. Explanation: Rating of how intact or uncorrupted the signal is. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighIntegrity'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldynamics|sigrecurr: Full name: 'Signal Recurrence'. Explanation: Whether the signal recurs over time. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: None, Regular, Sporadic.
column_meanings.alien|signaldynamics|sigevolve: Full name: 'Signal Evolution'. Explanation: Indicates if the signal changes/evolves during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Dynamic, Static, Unknown.
column_meanings.alien|signaldynamics|tempstab: Full name: 'Temporal Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal remains over time. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Stable'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldynamics|spatstab: Full name: 'Spatial Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal is spatially (e.g., consistent direction). Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Moderate'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldynamics|freqstab: Full name: 'Frequency Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal’s frequency is. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighlyStable'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldynamics|phasestab: Full name: 'Phase Stability'. Explanation: Any variation in signal phase. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'VaryingPhase'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldynamics|ampstab: Full name: 'Amplitude Stability'. Explanation: Consistency of signal amplitude. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Unstable'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldynamics|modstab: Full name: 'Modulation Stability'. Explanation: Consistency in the signal’s modulation scheme. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'Consistent'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldynamics|sigcoherence: Full name: 'Signal Coherence'. Explanation: How coherent the signal remains over its duration. Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighCoherence'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldynamics|sigdisp: Full name: 'Signal Dispersion'. Explanation: The degree to which the signal is dispersed (time/frequency smearing). Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'SignificantDisp'.
column_meanings.alien|signaldynamics|sigscint: Full name: 'Signal Scintillation'. Explanation: Fluctuation in signal amplitude due to propagation effects. Data type: VARCHAR(45). If no fixed categories, example: 'MildScintillation'.
column_meanings.alien|researchprocess|signalref: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-MNO-7890'.
column_meanings.alien|researchprocess|analysisprio: Full name: 'Analysis Priority'. Explanation: Priority assigned for analyzing this signal. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, Urgent.
column_meanings.alien|researchprocess|followstat: Full name: 'Follow-up Status'. Explanation: Status of any follow-up observations. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Required, Scheduled.
column_meanings.alien|researchprocess|peerrevstat: Full name: 'Peer Review Status'. Explanation: Where this signal stands in peer review. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, In Progress, Pending.
column_meanings.alien|researchprocess|pubstat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether findings about the signal have been published. Data type: CHAR(25). Possible categories: Draft, Published, Submitted.
column_meanings.alien|researchprocess|resprio: Full name: 'Research Priority'. Explanation: How urgently this signal needs scientific attention. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium.
column_meanings.alien|researchprocess|fundstat: Full name: 'Funding Status'. Explanation: Funding situation for further study. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Funded, Pending, Unfunded.

column_meanings.alien|researchprocess|secclass: Full name: 'Security Classification'. Explanation: Visibility and clearance level for the data. Data type: CHAR(35). Possible categories: Classified, Public, Restricted.
column_meanings.alien|researchprocess|discstat: Full name: 'Disclosure Status'. Explanation: How much information about the signal is shared publicly. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Full, None, Partial.
column_meanings.alien|researchprocess|notesmemo: Full name: 'Research Notes'. Explanation: Any extra remarks or context by researchers. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Project requires further funding...'

column_meanings.alien|observationalconditions|obstime: Full name: 'Observation Time'. Explanation: Local time of the observation in HH:MM:SS. Data type: TIME. Example: '13:45:59'.

column_meanings.alien|observationalconditions|obsdurhrs: Full name: 'Observation Duration (hours)'. Explanation: How long the observation lasted in hours. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '2.50'.

column_meanings.alien|sourceproperties|objtempk: Full name: 'Object Temperature (K)'. Explanation: Approximate surface temperature in Kelvin. Data type: INTEGER. Example: '5800'.

Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator (SNQI).description: Combines SNR and noise floor to provide a unified signal quality metric.
Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator (SNQI).definition: $\text{SNQI} = \text{SnrRatio} - 0.1 \times |\text{NoiseFloorDbm}|$, where higher values indicate better detection quality. Positive values generally indicate analyzable signals.

Atmospheric Observability Index (AOI).description: Quantifies how conducive atmospheric conditions are for signal detection.
Atmospheric Observability Index (AOI).definition: $\text{AOI} = \text{AtmosTransparency} \times (1 - \frac{\text{HumidityRate}}{100}) \times (1 - 0.02 \times \text{WindSpeedMs})$, where values closer to 1 indicate ideal observation conditions.

Signal Complexity Ratio (SCR).description: Measures the relationship between signal complexity and information density.
Signal Complexity Ratio (SCR).definition: $\text{SCR} = \frac{\text{ComplexIdx} \times \text{InfoDense}}{\log(\text{BwHz})}$, where higher values suggest potential artificial origin rather than natural phenomena.

Technological Origin Likelihood Score (T.description: Combines multiple factors to estimate likelihood of technological origin.
Technological Origin Likelihood Score (T.definition: $\text{TOLS} = \text{TechSigProb} \times (1 - \text{NatSrcProb}) \times \text{SigUnique} \times (0.5 + \frac{\text{AnomScore}}{10})$, where values above 0.75 warrant further investigation as potential technosignatures.

Bandwidth-Frequency Ratio (BFR).description: Measures the proportion of bandwidth to center frequency, helping identify signal type.
Bandwidth-Frequency Ratio (BFR).definition: $\text{BFR} = \frac{\text{BwHz}}{\text{CenterFreqMhz} \times 10^6}$, where narrow ratios ($<0.001$) often indicate technological signals while wider ratios suggest natural phenomena.

Detection Instrument Sensitivity Factor.description: Calculates the effective sensitivity of the detection setup based on telescope and environmental factors.
Detection Instrument Sensitivity Factor.definition: $\text{DISF} = (10 - \frac{|\text{AirTempC} - 15|}{10}) \times \text{AtmosTransparency} \times (1 - \frac{\text{HumidityRate}}{200}) \times \frac{100 - \text{LunarDistDeg}}{100}$, where values closer to 10 indicate optimal detection sensitivity.

Encoding Complexity Index (ECI).description: Evaluates the sophistication of potential encoding in the signal.
Encoding Complexity Index (ECI).definition: $\text{ECI} = \frac{\text{CompressRatio} \times \text{ComplexIdx} \times \text{EntropyVal}}{10}$, where values above 1.5 suggest deliberate information encoding rather than random patterns.

Signal Stability Metric (SSM).description: Quantifies overall temporal and spectral stability of a signal.
Signal Stability Metric (SSM).definition: $\text{SSM} = (1 - \frac{|\text{FreqDriftHzs}|}{\text{FreqMhz} \times 1000}) \times \frac{\text{SigDurSec}}{1 + \frac{\text{DoppShiftHz}}{1000}}$, where higher values indicate more stable signals typical of fixed transmitters.

Research Priority Index (RPI).description: Helps researchers prioritize signals for follow-up based on multiple factors.
Research Priority Index (RPI).definition: $\text{RPI} = (\text{TechSigProb} \times 4 + \frac{\text{BioSigProb}}{100} + \text{SigUnique} \times 2 + \frac{\text{AnomScore}}{2}) \times (1 - \text{FalsePosProb})$, where values above 3 indicate high research priority.

Lunar Interference Factor (LIF).description: Calculates the potential interference from lunar illumination on observations.
Lunar Interference Factor (LIF).definition: $\text{LIF} = (1 - \frac{\text{LunarDistDeg}}{180}) \times (1 - \text{AtmosTransparency})$, where higher values indicate more lunar interference. Values above 0.5 suggest significant lunar contamination in data.

Technosignature.description: Defines the concept of signals that indicate technological activity.
Technosignature.definition: A signal with $\text{TechSigProb} > 0.7$, $\text{NatSrcProb} < 0.3$, and $\text{ArtSrcProb} < 50$ that exhibits narrow bandwidth ($\text{BFR} < 0.001$) and high information density ($\text{InfoDense} > 0.8$).

Coherent Information Pattern (CIP).description: Identifies signals showing patterns consistent with deliberate information transmission.
Coherent Information Pattern (CIP).definition: Signals characterized by high signal stability ($\text{SSM} > 0.8$), organized information structure ($\text{EntropyVal}$ between 0.4-0.8), and consistent modulation ($\text{ModType}$ with $\text{ModIndex} > 0.5$).

Target of Opportunity (TOO).description: Identifies high-value signals requiring immediate follow-up observation.
Target of Opportunity (TOO).definition: Any signal with $\text{RPI} > 3.5$, $\text{TechSigProb} > 0.8$, and $\text{AnomScore} > 5$ that has not been previously documented or explained by known phenomena.

Optimal Observing Window (OOW).description: Defines conditions when observational quality is maximized.
Optimal Observing Window (OOW).definition: Time periods when $\text{AOI} > 0.85$, $\text{LunarStage}$ is 'New' or 'First Quarter', $\text{LunarDistDeg} > 45$, and $\text{SolarStatus}$ is 'Low' or 'Moderate'.

Signal Degradation Scenario (SDS).description: Characterizes situations where signal quality is compromised by environmental factors.
Signal Degradation Scenario (SDS).definition: Observation conditions where one or more of: $\text{AtmosTransparency} < 0.7$, $\text{HumidityRate} > 70$, $\text{WindSpeedMs} > 8$, or $\text{GeomagStatus}$ contains 'Storm', resulting in compromised data quality.

Narrowband Technological Marker (NTM).description: Identifies a specific signature associated with technological transmission.
Narrowband Technological Marker (NTM).definition: Signals with extremely narrow bandwidth ($\text{BFR} < 0.0001$), stable frequency ($\text{FreqDriftHzs} < 0.1$).

Observational Confidence Level (OCL).description: Rates the reliability of observations based on conditions and equipment.
Observational Confidence Level (OCL).definition: A classification system with three tiers: 'High' ($\text{AOI} > 0.8$, $\text{EquipStatus} = \text{'Operational'}$, $\text{CalibrStatus} = \text{'Current'}$), 'Medium' ($\text{AOI}$ 0.5-0.8, minor equipment issues), and 'Low' ($\text{AOI} < 0.5$ or significant equipment problems).

Potential Biosignature.description: Defines characteristics of signals potentially associated with biological processes.
Potential Biosignature.definition: Signals with $\text{BioSigProb} > 0.6$, $\text{TechSigProb} < 0.4$, and spectral features that match known biological emission patterns, often associated with specific molecular transitions.

Encoded Information Transfer (EIT).description: Characterizes signals that appear to contain deliberate information encoding.
Encoded Information Transfer (EIT).definition: Signals with $\text{ECI} > 1.8$, $\text{EntropyVal}$ between 0.3-0.7 (not random but structured), and consistent internal patterns that suggest language or data encoding schemes.

Fast Radio Transient (FRT).description: Defines a specific class of brief, high-energy radio emissions.
Fast Radio Transient (FRT).definition: Signals with extremely short duration ($\text{SigDurSec} < 0.1$), high signal strength ($\text{SigStrDb} > 15$), broad bandwidth ($\text{BwHz} > 1000000$), and no periodicity ($\text{RepeatCount} = 1$).

WeathProfile: Clear.description: Illustrates optimal weather conditions for signal detection.
WeathProfile: Clear.definition: Indicates pristine sky conditions with no clouds, usually associated with $\text{AtmosTransparency} > 0.9$, low $\text{HumidityRate} (< 40\%)$, and minimal $\text{WindSpeedMs} (< 3.0)$. Provides ideal visibility for optical observations and minimal atmospheric interference for radio observations.

SeeingProfile: Excellent.definition: Describes atmospheric conditions with minimal turbulence, allowing for sharp, detailed observations. Typically corresponds to image stability better than 1 arcsecond and is often associated with stable temperature gradients and low wind speeds ($\text{WindSpeedMs} < 2.5$).

SignalClass: Narrowband.description: Illustrates characteristics of narrowband signal detections.
SignalClass: Narrowband.definition: Describes signals occupying a very narrow portion of the spectrum (typically $\text{BFR} < 0.0001$). Often associated with technological origins as natural sources rarely produce such spectrally confined emissions. These signals are particularly interesting in SETI research.

GeomagStatus: Major Storm.definition: Indicates intense solar-induced geomagnetic activity with Kp index ≥ 7. During such conditions, ionospheric perturbations significantly affect radio observations below 100 MHz, aurora may be visible at mid-latitudes, and satellite communications may experience disruptions.

CIP Classification Label.description: Three-tier rating system for evaluating signal coherence against intelligent transmission criteria.
CIP Classification Label.definition: Classification labels: 'Coherent Information Pattern Detected' ($\text{SSM} > 0.8$, $\text{EntropyVal}$ between 0.4-0.8, and $\text{ModIndex} > 0.5$), 'Potential Information Pattern' ($\text{SSM} > 0.6$ and $\text{EntropyVal}$ between 0.3-0.9$), or 'No Clear Pattern' (all other signals).

SigClassType: Broadband Transient.description: Illustrates a class of brief signals covering wide frequency ranges.
SigClassType: Broadband Transient.definition: Describes short-duration signals ($\text{SigDurSec}$ typically $< 5$) that span a large portion of the spectrum ($\text{BFR} > 0.1$). Examples include solar radio bursts, lightning discharges, and certain types of cosmic explosions like Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs).

PolarMode: Circular.description: Illustrates circular polarization in detected signals.
PolarMode: Circular.definition: Describes electromagnetic waves where the electric field vector rotates in a circular pattern as the wave propagates. Circular polarization maintaining high purity across frequency (indicated by $\text{PolarAngleDeg}$ stability) is rare in natural sources and may indicate technological origin.

EncryptEvid: Strong Pattern.description: Illustrates characteristics suggesting deliberate signal encoding.
EncryptEvid: Strong Pattern.definition: Indicates detection of non-random, internally consistent patterns that resist simple decoding but show hallmarks of designed encryption or encoding. Characterized by high $\text{EntropyVal} (> 0.7)$ combined with structural regularity that defies natural explanation.

EncodeType: Frequency Hopping.description: Illustrates a sophisticated encoding method used in telecommunications.
EncodeType: Frequency Hopping.definition: Describes a transmission technique where the signal rapidly switches frequencies according to a predetermined sequence. Detection would be characterized by discontinuous spectral features that follow a pattern. This technique is used on Earth to secure communications and reduce interference.

FalsePosProb: <0.01.description: Illustrates extremely high confidence in signal detection.
FalsePosProb: <0.01.definition: Indicates less than 1% probability that the signal is a false detection or artifact. Such low false positive probability typically results from multiple independent confirmations, excellent signal strength (high $\text{SnrRatio}$), and elimination of all known terrestrial and instrumental sources.

Modulation Complexity Score (MCS).description: Quantifies the sophistication of signal modulation based on type and stability.
Modulation Complexity Score (MCS).definition: $\text{MCS} = \text{ModIndex} \times (1 + \text{SSM}) \times M_{\text{factor}}$, where $M_{\text{factor}}$ is 2 for $\text{ModType} = \text{'AM'}$, 1.5 for 'FM', and 1 for other types. Incorporates Signal Stability Metric (SSM) to weight stable modulations higher.

Artificial Intelligence Detection Probab.description: Calculates likelihood of artificial intelligence origin based on encoding complexity and technosignature indicators.
Artificial Intelligence Detection Probab.definition: $\text{AIDP} = \frac{\text{ECI} \times \text{TOLS}}{1 + \text{NatSrcProb}}$, where ECI (Encoding Complexity Index) and TOLS (Technological Origin Likelihood Score) are weighted against natural source probability.

Observation Quality Factor (OQF).description: Provides a comprehensive measure of observational conditions quality.
Observation Quality Factor (OQF).definition: $\text{OQF} = \text{AOI} \times (1 - \text{LIF}) \times (\text{PointAccArc} < 2 ? 1 : \frac{2}{\text{PointAccArc}})$, where AOI (Atmospheric Observability Index) and LIF (Lunar Interference Factor) are combined with telescope pointing accuracy.

Information Entropy Ratio (IER).description: Compares signal entropy to expected natural background entropy.
Information Entropy Ratio (IER).definition: $\text{IER} = \frac{\text{EntropyVal}}{\text{NatSrcProb} \times 0.9 + 0.1}$, where values significantly greater than 1 suggest non-natural information content. Uses NatSrcProb as a baseline for expected natural entropy.

Signal Processing Efficiency Index (SPEI.description: Evaluates the computational efficiency of signal processing relative to complexity.
Signal Processing Efficiency Index (SPEI.definition: $\text{SPEI} = \frac{\text{DecodeIters} \times \text{ProcTimeHrs}}{\text{ECI} \times \text{ComplexIdx}}$, where ECI (Encoding Complexity Index) provides the complexity component to normalize processing time and iterations.

Celestial Location Significance Factor (.description: Calculates significance of signal source location based on astronomical targets of interest.
Celestial Location Significance Factor (.definition: $\text{CLSF} = (\text{CelestObj} ? 2 : 1) \times (\text{ObjType} == \text{'Giant'} \&\& \text{ObjMassSol} \text{ between } 0.8 \text{ and } 1.2 ? 1.5 : 1) \times (\text{ObjMetal} > 0 ? \text{ObjMetal} + 1 : 0.5)$, where higher values indicate source locations more likely to harbor intelligent life.

Confirmation Confidence Score (CCS).description: Quantifies overall confidence in signal verification across multiple parameters.
Confirmation Confidence Score (CCS).definition: $\text{CCS} = (1 - \text{FalsePosProb}) \times \text{DecodeConf} \times \text{ClassConf} \times (\text{SNQI} > 0 ? \frac{\text{SNQI}}{10} + 0.5 : 0.1)$, where SNQI (Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator) provides a quality weighting factor.

Habitable Zone Signal Relevance (HZSR).description: Assesses signal relevance based on source's position in habitable zone.
Habitable Zone Signal Relevance (HZSR).definition: $\text{HZSR} = \text{TOLS} \times (\text{ObjType} == \text{'Dwarf'} ? (0.7 \leq \text{ObjMassSol} \leq 1.4 ? (0.8 \leq \frac{\text{SourceDistLy}}{\sqrt{\text{ObjMassSol}}} \leq 1.7 ? 2 : 0.5) : 0.3) : 0.1)$, where TOLS (Technological Origin Likelihood Score) is weighted by stellar habitability factors.

Pattern Recognition Confidence (PRC).description: Measures confidence in identified signal patterns based on multiple factors.
Pattern Recognition Confidence (PRC).definition: $\text{PRC} = (\text{RepeatCount} > 1 ? 1 + \log_{10}(\text{RepeatCount}) : 0.5) \times (\text{EntropyVal} < 0.9 ? 1 : 0.3) \times \text{SCR}$, where SCR (Signal Complexity Ratio) provides complexity weighting.

NTM Classification System.description: A tiered classification system for Narrowband Technological Markers based on signal characteristics.
NTM Classification System.definition: Three-tier classification: 'Strong NTM' (BFR < 0.0001 AND FreqDriftHzs < 0.1 AND non-natural modulation), 'Moderate NTM' (BFR < 0.0005 AND FreqDriftHzs < 0.5 AND non-natural modulation), and 'Not NTM' (all other signals).

High-Confidence Technosignature.description: Defines signals with extremely high likelihood of technological origin.
High-Confidence Technosignature.definition: A Technosignature with $\text{CCS} > 0.9$, $\text{MCS} > 1.5$, and $\text{AIDP} > 0.8$, indicating a signal that meets the basic Technosignature criteria with additional confirmation through modulation complexity and artificial intelligence detection markers.

Habitable Zone Transmission.description: Identifies signals originating from stellar habitable zones with technological characteristics.
Habitable Zone Transmission.definition: A signal with $\text{HZSR} > 1.5$ and Technosignature characteristics, originating from a star system with conditions potentially suitable for life, making it a priority candidate for SETI research.

Multi-Channel Communication Protocol.description: Identifies signal patterns consistent with sophisticated communication protocols.
Multi-Channel Communication Protocol.definition: Signal exhibiting Coherent Information Pattern (CIP) characteristics across multiple frequency channels with coordinated timing ($\text{RepeatCount} > 3$, $\text{PeriodSec}$ consistent across observations) and $\text{ECI} > 2.0$, suggesting a designed communication system.

Quantum-Coherent Transmission.description: Describes signals potentially employing quantum properties for communication.
Quantum-Coherent Transmission.definition: Signals with $\text{QuantEffects}$ containing 'Significant' or 'Observed' patterns, exhibiting unusually high information density ($\text{InfoDense} > 1.5$) while maintaining an $\text{ECI} > 2.5$, suggesting advanced transmission technologies beyond conventional radiofrequency methods.

Research Critical Signal.description: Defines signals requiring immediate and extensive scientific resources.
Research Critical Signal.definition: Signals meeting Target of Opportunity (TOO) criteria with additional $\text{PRC} > 0.8$ and $\text{IMDF} < 0.5$, indicating high-quality, minimally distorted signals that show recognizable patterns warranting priority allocation of research resources.

Directed Transmission.description: Identifies signals that appear specifically directed rather than omnidirectional.
Directed Transmission.definition: Signals with high spatial stability ($\text{SpatStab} = \text{'Moderate'}$), narrow beam characteristics ($\text{PolarMode} = \text{'Linear'}$ with stable $\text{PolarAngleDeg}$), and high $\text{TOLS} > 0.85$, suggesting intentional transmission toward our location.

Signal of Galactic Significance.description: Classifies signals with potential importance to galactic civilization models.
Signal of Galactic Significance.definition: Signals originating from regions of high $\text{CLSF} (> 2.0)$ that display Technosignature characteristics and have $\text{AIDP} > 0.7$, representing potential evidence of advanced civilizations at galactic-relevant locations.

CCS Approximation.description: Simplified CCS calculation using direct signal-to-noise ratio values when full Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator (SNQI) data is unavailable.

Observation-Verified Signal.description: Defines signals that have undergone rigorous verification processes.
Observation-Verified Signal.definition: Signals observed under Optimal Observing Window (OOW) conditions with $\text{OQF} > 0.85$ and $\text{CCS} > 0.8$, indicating high-quality observations with multiple verification methods applied.

Anomalous Quantum Signal.description: Describes signals exhibiting quantum properties inconsistent with current physics models.
Anomalous Quantum Signal.definition: Signals with $\text{QuantEffects}$ indicating anomalous behavior, $\text{AnomScore} > 8$, and unusually high $\text{MCS} (> 2.0)$, suggesting either unknown natural quantum phenomena or extremely advanced transmission technologies beyond current human capabilities.

Analyzable Signals.description: Signals of sufficient quality to be considered useful for further analysis.
Analyzable Signals.definition: Signals with SNQI > 0 are considered analyzable.

Bandwidth-to-Frequency Ratio (BFR).description: Normalized signal width relative to its central frequency.
Bandwidth-to-Frequency Ratio (BFR).definition: $\text{BFR} = \frac{\text{BwHz}}{\text{CenterFreqMhz} \times 1{,}000{,}000}$, used to characterize signal spread relative to its frequency band.

TOLS Category.description: Classification of signals based on TOLS thresholds.
TOLS Category.definition: Categorized as 'Low' if TOLS < 0.25, 'Medium' if TOLS < 0.75, and 'High' otherwise.

High Lunar Interference Events.definition: Events where the calculated LIF is greater than 0.5, indicating strong lunar contamination in the data.

High Confidence Signals.description: Signal with Confirmation Confidence Score (CCS) > 0.8, indicating high reliability.

Equipment Problems.description: Defines what counts as an abnormal condition for a telescope’s subsystems.
Equipment Problems.definition: A telescope is considered to have an equipment problem whenever **any** of its key subsystem states are not in their nominal condition: • Equipment status is not “Operational”; • Calibration status is not “Current”; • Cooling-system status is not “Normal”.

-- alien_5.sql
-- Breakdown of signal modulation types with at least 5 occurrences.
-- For each modulation type: modulation type, signal count, average MCS, average SNR,
-- and a JSON with per-signal MCS and SNR values.
--
-- MCS = ModIndex * (1 + SSM) * M_factor
-- SSM = (1 - |FreqDriftHzs| / (FreqMhz * 1000)) * (SigDurSec / (1 + DoppShiftHz / 1000))
-- M_factor: 2 for AM, 1.5 for FM, 1 for other

SELECT s.ModType, COUNT(*) AS signal_count,
    AVG(s.ModIndex * (1 + (1 - ABS(s.FreqDriftHzs)/(s.FreqMhz*1000)) * s.SigDurSec/(1 + s.DoppShiftHz/1000)) *
        CASE WHEN s.ModType = 'AM' THEN 2 WHEN s.ModType = 'FM' THEN 1.5 ELSE 1 END) AS avg_mcs,
    AVG(s.SnrRatio) AS avg_snr,
    JSON_GROUP_OBJECT(
        s.SignalRegistry,
        JSON_OBJECT(
            'mcs', s.ModIndex * (1 + (1 - ABS(s.FreqDriftHzs)/(s.FreqMhz*1000)) * s.SigDurSec/(1 + s.DoppShiftHz/1000)) *
                   CASE WHEN s.ModType = 'AM' THEN 2 WHEN s.ModType = 'FM' THEN 1.5 ELSE 1 END,
            'snr', s.SnrRatio
        )
    ) AS signal_details
FROM Signals s
WHERE s.ModType IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.ModType
HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;

query: Which observatories have the most promising signals worth investigating? I need a summary by observatory showing the observatory name, their total signal count, average Research Priority Index (RPI) and approximate Confirmation Confidence Score (CCS) values, number of high-priority (RPI > 3) signals, number of high-confidence signals, and especially the number of signals that meet both criteria. Sort the results by observatories with the most high-priority-and-high-confidence signals first.
sol_sql: WITH priority_calc AS ( SELECT s.SignalRegistry, ( p.TechSigProb * 4 + p.BioSigProb / 100 + p.SigUnique * 2 + p.AnomScore / 2 ) * ( 1 - p.FalsePosProb ) AS RPI, ( 1 - p.FalsePosProb ) * d.DecodeConf * ( CASE WHEN s.SnrRatio - 0.1 * ABS(s.NoiseFloorDbm) > 0 THEN ( s.SnrRatio - 0.1 * ABS(s.NoiseFloorDbm) ) / 10 + 0.5 ELSE 0.1 END ) AS CCS_approx, o.ObservStation FROM Signals AS s JOIN SignalProbabilities AS p ON s.SignalRegistry = p.SignalRef JOIN SignalDecoding AS d ON s.SignalRegistry = d.SignalRef JOIN Telescopes AS t ON s.TelescRef = t.TelescRegistry JOIN Observatories AS o ON t.ObservStation = o.ObservStation ) SELECT ObservStation, COUNT(*) AS signal_count, AVG(RPI) AS avg_rpi, AVG(CCS_approx) AS avg_ccs, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE RPI > 3) AS high_priority_signals, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE CCS_approx > 0.8) AS high_confidence_signals, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE RPI > 3 AND CCS_approx > 0.8) AS high_priority_high_confidence FROM priority_calc GROUP BY ObservStation ORDER BY high_priority_high_confidence DESC NULLS FIRST
